review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp attributes against the definitions. I also compared them with the analogous `Finpartition` simp lemmas and with `Set.bot_eq_empty` and `Set.sSup_eq_sUnion`. The two findings below are the only ones I could support from the sources. The simp lemmas `sSup_eq` and `sUnion_eq` are coherent: `Set.sSup_eq_sUnion` is simp, so `sUnion_eq` is the lemma that fires for set partitions. The `rel_comm` lemma is correctly left non-simp because it would loop. I did not run Lean. Whether `bot_notMem` fails to fire on `∅ ∈ P` is my inference from the different head symbols (`Bot.bot` versus `EmptyCollection.emptyCollection`) and the simp attribute on `Set.bot_eq_empty`, not something I observed.

findings.problem: For `P : Partition u` with `u : Set α`, the simp-normal form of the bottom element is `∅`. `Set.bot_eq_empty` is a simp lemma, so simp rewrites `⊥` to `∅`. The generic simp lemma `bot_notMem : ⊥ ∉ P` has the head symbol `Bot.bot`. It will not be matched by the discrimination tree against a goal `∅ ∈ P`, which has head `EmptyCollection.emptyCollection`. The set-specialised `empty_notMem` is the lemma that would close such goals, but it lacks `@[simp]`. As a result the simp set has no rule for the normal form `∅ ∈ P` of set partitions. The file itself shows the friction: `nonempty_of_mem` has to convert from `⊥` to `∅` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`, as `Finpartition.empty_notMem_parts` already is: `@[simp] lemma empty_notMem : ∅ ∉ P := P.bot_notMem`.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then discharge `∅ ∈ P` and `∅ ∈ P.parts`-style side goals for set partitions. Without it, such goals only work after an explicit `rw` or a manual `P.bot_notMem`. This also parallels the existing `Finpartition` interface.

findings.excerpt: lemma partOf_nonempty_iff : (P.partOf x).Nonempty ↔ x ∈ u := by
findings.problem: The sibling `partOf_eq_empty_iff` is a simp lemma, and it is derived from this one. `partOf_nonempty_iff` is not simp. So `simp` normalises `P.partOf x = ∅` to `x ∉ u`, but leaves `(P.partOf x).Nonempty` untouched. The same fact then has two different normal forms depending on how it is phrased. `Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty` can also push `¬ Nonempty` to `= ∅`, but a positive `Nonempty` goal has no simp route to `x ∈ u`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `partOf_nonempty_iff`, so that `(P.partOf x).Nonempty` rewrites to `x ∈ u`. It is an unconditional iff with a strictly simpler right-hand side, and no existing simp lemma has a competing left-hand side. It combines safely with `partOf_eq_empty_iff`.
findings.benefit: The `Nonempty` and `= ∅` phrasings then simplify consistently to membership in the support `u`. Users no longer need to rewrite with the lemma by hand.
